description: vanilla is a minimalist, high-performance HTTP server written in V: multi-threaded, non-blocking epoll I/O, lock-free, copy-free, SO_REUSEPORT. Handlers are pure (request)->[]u8 returning raw response bytes. JSON is built in a single allocation with precomputed prefixes (no per-request reflection); json-comp gzips on Accept-Encoding; json-tls terminates TLS 1.3 (Mbed TLS 4) on :8081 with ALPN http/1.1, reusing the same allocation-free /json serializer; static-tls serves the 20 /static files on :8081 through vanilla's static_assets (br/gzip negotiation; snapshots re-checked against the disk, so a replaced file is served at once), sending bodies of 16 KiB or more with sendfile(2) over kTLS; fortunes renders the DB rows + a runtime row with HTML escaping; async-db/crud/fortunes use the native async pg_async driver with per-worker pipelined pools. Pinned V master (built from source, bootstrap pinned). async parks each /delay/{ms} on a one-shot timerfd from a per-worker free-list and answers only once it reports an expiration; 8gbit echoes the POST body on the :8081 TLS listener (Content-Length or chunked, per-worker dechunk buffer); production-stack's /api cache-aside (X-Cache MISS/HIT, 1 s items / 30 s users TTL, invalidated on write) runs in-process — no Redis required. The h2c profiles run on an h2c-only epoll listener on :8082 (an HTTP/1.1 request there gets 505): the connection preface (PRI *) parses as an ordinary request, the handler hands the connection to vanilla's http2 module (core.queue_takeover) and appends the server SETTINGS, and every later burst goes to the RFC 9113 machine, which surfaces a request only when it is complete; /json reuses the same prefixes and body writer. unary-grpc takes the same preface on :8080 and answers GetSum as HEADERS, the SumReply as DATA, then grpc-status 0 as trailers. The echo-ws profiles share the :8080 engine: GET /ws validates the RFC 6455 upgrade, appends the 101 and hands the connection over (core.queue_takeover), after which every readable burst goes to a ConnHandler that walks the frames (echo, ping/pong, close) instead of the HTTP/1.1 parser; a pipelined burst is drained in one call and coalesced into one write, and the accept key is computed on the stack, so an upgrade allocates nothing. One worker per CPU of the container's cpuset.
